key_insight: A training-free, zero-shot 3D anomaly detection method can localize lesions by turning 2D foundation model slice features into volumetric tokens and flagging subjects whose tokens have no close matches across the batch.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help identify abnormal regions in heterogeneous 3D medical scans when labeled 3D training data are scarce, especially for new or rare pathologies.
method: Decompose each 3D volume along multiple anatomical axes and encode slices with a frozen 2D vision transformer.
Pool neighboring slice features into localized volumetric tokens for cross-subject comparison.
Use coarse-to-fine tokenization to preserve focal lesion signals while avoiding exhaustive matching.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on brain MRI for metastases, glioma, and stroke, with additional validation on lung CT to assess generalizability beyond atlas-aligned brain imaging.
watch_item: Performance may drop when lesions are low-contrast or when depth pooling attenuates small focal abnormalities, so token resolution and modality matter.
paper_title: Toward Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in 3D Medical Images: A Batch-Based Approach Using 2D Foundation Models
